conviction_note: Evidence is close to balanced: a 4-for-4 record of revenue beats against a consensus that sits exactly at the guide midpoint, plus 13.5% of shares short at ~10 days to cover, on one side; a 10.5% 5-day run-up, decelerating OUS (+4.4% in Q2, guide implies negative H2) and the last beat-and-raise being sold -13% on the other. Findings sum +1.0; scaled number (2x0.52-1)x10 = +0.4. p_up was cut from 53 to 52 because a long lean runs against +17 vol points of put skew and a 5.5 put/call OI ratio; the gap between the two measurements is that skew haircut, not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $66.6M, non-GAAP EPS -$0.24 (Benzinga consensus via search snippet, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESTA/earnings-forecasts; Korean mirror $66.7M/-$0.25; TickFlow ~$65M/-$0.27, https://www.tickflow.io/stock/ESTA/forecast). Cross-check against company guide: FY26 $269-271M (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/establishment-labs-establishment-labs-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-20260806) less H1 $127.3M implies H2 $141.7-143.7M; Benzinga Q3 $66.6M + Q4 $76.2M = $142.8M, i.e. consensus sits at the guide midpoint. Bar treated as sourced (two roughly agreeing estimate sources plus guide arithmetic).
positioning_check: Short interest 4,017,107 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 13.5% of 29.8M shares outstanding (float smaller, so % of float higher), days to cover 9.77; was 3.98M on 09-30 and 4.40M on 08-31, range-bound, well below the 5.22M March peak (https://equibles.com/stocks/esta/shortinterest). Baseline: 25d skew +16.97 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI ratio 5.47 on 5,005 contracts, ATM legs not two-sided so no implied move; 5d run-up +10.53%, 20d +7.27%, 28% below 52w high. Read: put-heavy and a crowded short on a name that has already bounced ~10% off the 10-19 low; a squeeze mechanism exists on a beat, the skew says the market is paying for a repeat of August.

findings.finding: Consensus for Q3 revenue ($66.6M) plus Q4 ($76.2M) equals $142.8M, exactly the midpoint of the H2 the FY26 guide implies ($141.7-143.7M after H1 $127.3M), while ESTA has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last several quarters (Q1'26 +4.2% at $59.88M vs $57.48M, Q4'25 +0.8%, Q3'25 +3.1%); a repeat 2-4% beat ($68-69M) would sit above the guided path and likely bring a third raise of the FY range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat-and-raise has been paid unevenly: Q3'25 beat and raise +22.49% (2025-11-05), Q4'25 +6.28%, Q1'26 beat +5.0%, but Q2'26 beat ($67.5M, +31.7%) with a $2.5M raise fell -13.37% (2026-08-06) on a wider EPS loss and OUS deceleration.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is pinned to the guide midpoint rather than to the company's beat habit; if the street were anticipating a beat-and-raise, Q3 estimates would sit above $67.5M (Q2's level, with management saying US strength continued into Q3) rather than below it, and the skew would not be +17 points to the downside.
findings.independence: Consensus figures from Benzinga forecast page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESTA/earnings-forecasts, via snippet) and TickFlow (https://www.tickflow.io/stock/ESTA/forecast); Q2 call says momentum continued 'into the third quarter' (https://www.webull.com/news/15700165989565440). Shares the Q2 release with the OUS and FCF findings.

findings.finding: Outside the US the business is stalling: Q2 OUS revenue was $42.8M, +4.4% YoY (Q1'26 ~+14%), Middle East orders were 'well below past levels', and with US at ~$26M/quarter the FY guide implies H2 OUS of ~$86.7M against $89.2M in H2'25 (about -3%); management called Q3 'historically the softest quarter' with OUS following its normal summer pattern, so a negative OUS growth print in Q3 is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: OUS deceleration was a named driver of the -13.37% reaction to Q2 on 2026-08-06 and of the sell-off TD Cowen called overdone on 2026-10-19.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the August sell-off and the put skew already reflect it. What is not priced is the size of the Q3 OUS number, which lands in the softest seasonal quarter; net of the US business (37% of revenue, +141% in Q2), a -3% OUS print is roughly what the guide already embeds, so only a print worse than that moves the stock.
findings.independence: Goldesel 2026-10-19 says investors focused on slowing non-US momentum that 'could even turn negative in H2' (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/establishment-labs-holdings-aktie-td-cowen-halt-abverkauf-fur-uberzogen); OUS split computed from the release (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/establishment-labs-establishment-labs-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-results-20260806).

findings.finding: AbbVie's US 'Other Aesthetics' line, which is the only line that can hold Natrelle breast implants, fell 8.3% YoY in Q2 2026 to $258M while ESTA's US revenue rose 141%, consistent with Motiva taking US share from the incumbent; the same filing shows US Juvederm -2.0% and the 10-Q cites lower consumer demand, so the aesthetic market itself is soft.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: US Motiva revenue has been the line ESTA trades up on: Q3'25 US $11.9M beat +22.49%; Q1'26 US $19.6M +5.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a competitor's line that does not name implants and has been public since July; it bears on whether US share gains continue in Q3, but AbbVie's Q3 figures come after this window. Proxy only.
findings.independence: Proxy; AbbVie 10-Q notes Juvederm decline on lower consumer demand (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001551152/000155115226000026/abbv-20260630.htm), which points the other way for market size.

findings.finding: Short interest is 4.02M shares (13.5% of shares outstanding, more of float) with 9.77 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement, alongside a 5.47 put/call open-interest ratio: downside is crowded into a print where the company has beaten revenue four quarters running, so a clean beat has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 print (beat and raise, Nov 2025) produced +22.49%, the largest move in the 8-print history, from a similarly heavy short base (5.22M peak at 2026-03-31).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is visible to anyone, but it is a mechanism rather than a fact the price absorbs; if the shorts had covered into the print, the 09-30 to 10-15 settlements would show a falling count, and they show +34k.
findings.independence: Baseline put/call OI 5.47 and skew +16.97 (sealed baseline file) point to the same crowded downside.

findings.finding: The stock has already rebounded +10.5% in five sessions to $68.84 from roughly $61 (EUR 52.52) on 2026-10-19, the day TD Cowen called the sell-off overdone, so part of the 'oversold into a beat' setup has been bought before the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 came after the stock had held in the high-70s and fell -13.37%; no clean history of run-up-then-print on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself; filed because it raises the bar a beat must clear. If the run-up reflected leaked strength it would be accompanied by estimate revisions upward, and no Q3 estimate change was found.

findings.finding: 8-K filed 2026-10-15: Amendment No. 3 to the NuSil Master Supply Agreement (medical-grade silicone, ESTA's key raw material) extends the term from 2026-12-31 to 2031-12-31 effective 2027-01-01, with amended pricing, payment and business-continuity provisions (pricing redacted).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction to a supply-agreement disclosure on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: A quiet 8-K with redacted pricing; the call is the first chance for management to say whether the new pricing helps or hurts 2027 gross margin (70.6% in Q2). Removes a single-source expiry risk that ended this year.

findings.finding: Management promised a transition to free-cash-flow positive in H2 2026, but H1 operating cash flow was -$20.9M with capex $5.5M (FCF about -$26.4M), net debt to Oaktree $261.7M carries ~$7.0M quarterly interest, and Q3 is the seasonally softest quarter; a still-negative Q3 FCF or a wider GAAP loss would repeat the line the August print was sold on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: revenue beat and raise but GAAP loss of $0.39/share, wider than expected per secondary sources, and the stock fell -13.37%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS (-$0.24) is visible but the cash-flow line is not carried in estimates; the FCF claim is a promise for H2 as a whole, so Q3 can miss it without breaking guidance. The financing itself was a refinancing (borrowed $265M, repaid $246.4M) that funds a growing US business, not distress, and management says no equity raise is needed.
findings.independence: Walnut Invest attributes the August drop to a wider-than-expected loss (https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/esta). Shares the Q2 release with finding 1.

findings.finding: The Brazilian real was materially stronger in mid-2026 than a year earlier (EUR per BRL 0.1715 on 2026-06-02 vs 0.1538 a year before; EUR/BRL 5.78-6.07 in July-August 2026), a reported-revenue tailwind for ESTA's Latin American OUS sales in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Company does not quantify FX; no reaction history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed; sell-side models do not necessarily mark FX in-quarter. Small proxy.
findings.independence: YoY BRL/EUR figure from https://ycharts.com/indicators/brazilian_real_to_euro_exchange_rate (snippet); proxy, unconfirmed by the company.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management previewed 2027 revenue growth of 'around 25%' without formal guidance; the Q3 call is the next chance to firm or qualify it, against a FY26 guide of $270M (so ~$337M for 2027).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No formal next-year guide has been given at a Q3 print before; the January JPM pre-announcement (2026-01-12) moved -2.31%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 25% figure was a verbal aside in Q&A, not guidance; whether consensus 2027 sits there was not verifiable. A firmed number in a soft OUS environment would be new information either way.

findings.finding: The FDA review of Motiva for primary and revision breast reconstruction (submitted December 2025) is still open: on the Q2 call management said it was answering 'routine questions' and expects no material recon revenue until 2028; TD Cowen on 2026-10-19 framed approval as a significant additional market. Any approval or update on the Q3 call is upside the stock does not carry.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The original US augmentation approval (2024-09-27) was the company's defining re-rating; no recon-specific reaction yet.
findings.why_not_priced: No date has been set, so the market assigns little probability to news inside this window; the expected value is small because the probability is small, not because the event would be.

outside_window.finding: AbbVie's Q3 2026 aesthetics release (the incumbent breast-implant maker's US Other Aesthetics line) is expected late October, likely after this window; it would be the first counterparty read on Q3 US share shift.
Short interest for the 2026-10-30 settlement (published 2026-11-10) will show whether shorts covered into or after the print.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly long, which cuts against +17 vol points of put skew and a 5.5 put/call OI ratio and comes after a 10.5% 5-day run-up; the reason not to defer fully to the skew is a 13.5% short base at ~10 days to cover on a company that has beaten revenue four quarters running against a consensus pinned to the guide midpoint, but that is enough only for p_up 52, not more.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding cut from +1.5 to +1.0 because the last beat-and-raise was sold -13.37%.

Lesson 7 (positioning): long lean runs against +17 skew, so p_up cut from 53 to 52; the crowded short (13.5% of shares, 9.8 DTC) shrank the three negatives (OUS -1.0 to -0.8, run-up -0.8 to -0.6, FCF -0.7 to -0.5).
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): AbbVie Other Aesthetics proxy cut from +0.3 to +0.2, BRL FX proxy from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Oaktree refinancing was read as funding the US ramp with no equity need, so it is not a separate negative; only the FCF/EPS line remains, sized small.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): bar sourced to two estimate sources plus guide arithmetic; consensus equals the guide midpoint, so a beat lands outside what the company guided. No cap applied.
Lesson 9 (net of segment): OUS finding sized net of a US business at 37% of revenue growing 141%, against the -3% H2 OUS the guide already embeds; left at -0.8.
